Public model-card and AI-risk guidance also support a monitored-launch approach with explicit disclosure of limitations and ongoing measurement. The unresolved issue is confined to the clinical coding assistant slice, concentrated in observation-status guidance, and the draft runbook is not mature enough to eliminate disclosure obligations because owner and alert threshold remain TBD. output.claims_about_policy: The governing policy text is narrower than the audited claim appears to assume. It allows certification without material caveats only if there is current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show that predicate has been met. At the same time, the policy does not bar certification with a disclosed limitation; it bars treating draft monitoring artifacts as a substitute for the required disclosure or approved mitigation. Public governance guidance supports the structure of a disclosed, monitored launch, but does not replace the internal release-policy requirement.
